title: Plano de Manila y sus arrabales (Francisco J. de Gamoneda, 1898), 1:10,000; and the War Department reissue "Manila y sus arrabales, to accompany Report of Major General Commanding for 1898" (Norris Peters)
holder: University of Minnesota (umedia p16022coll205:757); University of Texas, Perry-Castaneda Library ("Manila 1898"); Wikimedia Commons "Manila and suburbs 1898.jpg"
what it holds: A surveyed Spanish city plan of 1898 at 1:10,000: streets, esteros, the shore front and the walls in detail, from San Nicolas to Pasay. An independent check on the reconstructed shoreline and street lines
access: Online
rights: Published 1898; the reissue is a US Government publication: public domain
notes: Not used yet. The best second map for a person to check the reconstruction against. USED 21 Nov 2026 for a check, not for any line: the traced shore, walls, Pasig and main roads were laid on the 1,280-px copy by two landmarks both maps draw as rings (Bilibid prison, Paco cemetery). By eye they agree to about 20-30 m along Tondo, San Nicolas, Ermita and Malate and at the walls. West of the Walled City they cannot be compared: the plan draws the port then planned, not the shore. pipeline/recon/manila_1899_check_1898.md.

title: Manila y sus arrabales: "To accompany Report of the Major General Commanding for 1898" (War Department reissue of the Spanish plan, with the blockhouse line numbered)
holder: Yale University, Beinecke Library; image 15249769 of Yale Digital Collections (seen through Yale-NUS historical maps, record beinecke-15249769)
what it holds: Black line print, 56 x 29 cm, north at the top, with latitude and longitude ticks. The city and the suburbs from Tondo to well south of Malate: Ermita, Malate, Paco, Singalong, the shore, the roads towards Pasay, the Estero Tripa de Gallina, marsh, and the old Spanish blockhouse line with its numbers (12, 13 and 14 seen). Scan 4,551 x 7,118 px, served as zoomable tiles (IIIF level 2: https://collections.library.yale.edu/iiif/2/15249769).
access: Scan fetched 21 Nov 2026 (4,551 x 7,118 px) once the Yale image host was allowed; fitted and read.
rights: A US War Department publication of 1898: public domain as a US government work. Yale's own rights statement was not found (the catalogue page is not under the image's number); to be confirmed.
notes: The map to trace the south from: it carries the shore, roads and blockhouses 12 to 14 that the engineer map (S78) stops short of, and its own graticule to fit it by. It shows the ground as of 1898, six months before the battle. Two other Yale sheets were opened and set aside: "Manila" (1899, The Philippines Company, 41 x 31 cm, image 15249770), a commercial plan that ends at Malate; and "Manila, sus arrabales" (1900, north-east sheet of several, coloured, image 15249771), which by its record does not reach south of about 14.559 N.
